title: Labeler heuristic cascade notebook
content:
Purpose:
This is a personal scratchpad for designing a compact, testable cascade of labeling heuristics and fallbacks for messy metadata fields. The goal is to capture rule priority, conflict resolution, and quick regex/snippet examples so reviewers can run a small triage pass before full adjudication.

Context / problem statement:
- Many records have partial or contradictory metadata (e.g., source title vs. extracted filename vs. user-entered subtitle).
- We want a cheap, deterministic pass that: 1) resolves high-confidence cases automatically, 2) flags medium-confidence for fast human review, 3) leaves low-confidence untouched for full adjudication.
- Keep rules explainable and reversible (store which rule applied).

High-level cascade (first pass ordering):
1) Canonical extraction from trusted structured fields (KMS-like canonical_title, url_title) — accept if non-empty and matches normalization checks.
2) Timestamp-based inference — prefer explicit date fields if within expected window.
3) Dominant token vote across fields (slug/filename/ocr/transcription) — if same token appears 2+ times across different sources, accept.
4) Heuristic expansions (abbrev expansion, punctuation squash) — apply only if result improves token match confidence by >= 0.2.
5) ML fallback: small scoring model (logistic) trained on adjudicated set — only used to score ambiguous but non-sensitive fields.
6) Manual flag (low confidence) — surface to human queue.

Example rule details (title-like field):
- Rule: "punctuation-squash (priority 4)"
  - Intent: strip surrounding quotes, trailing punctuation, double spaces, unicode ‘smart’ quotes -> straight quotes.
  - Regex / transforms: s/[‘’“”]/' /g ; s/[\s]+/ /g ; trim leading/trailing ["'`.,:-]+
  - Confidence bump: +0.1 if result length >= 4 and contains alphanumeric
  - Danger: collapses legitimate punctuation (e.g., "C++") — add exception list: ["C++","R&D","e.g."]

- Rule: "abbrev-expand (priority 5)"
  - Small mapping table (abbr -> expansion): {"svc":"service","mnt":"mount","intl":"international"} — only apply if expansion appears in corpus frequency > 50 and original token freq < 5
  - Note: add audit tag when expansion applied.

Conflict resolution patterns:
- If two rules give different non-empty outputs, produce: resolved_value + meta.rule_applied (primary_rule) + meta.confidence_delta and then compare confidence scores.
- If confidence difference < 0.05, mark as "ambiguous_pair" and push to quick-review bucket with top-3 alternatives.

Quick examples (real-ish noisy inputs):
1) filename: "Q4_sales-report_final (1).pdf" ; extracted title: "Q4 Sales Report" -> apply punctuation-squash, remove parenthetical counters, normalize case -> PASS auto-accept (rule 1->3 chain).
2) ocr_text: "Dr. M. O'Leary — CEO" ; name field later shows "Michael OLeary" -> apply abbrev expansion? no. Use dominant token vote -> "O'Leary" wins. Note: retain original punctuation as alias.
3) title: "AI R&D: results" vs metadata: "AI Research & Development" -> map ampersand/and variants and abbreviation expansions; if mapping yields exact match, unify and add audit tag.

Small scoring pseudocode (for fallback model):
- features: token_overlap_ratio, avg_token_freq_in_corpus, presence_in_trusted_field, edit_distance_min, punctuation_squash_applied
- score -> logistic -> threshold 0.78 auto-accept, 0.45-0.78 quick-review, <0.45 manual

Audit & provenance:
- Every automatic change must record: original_value, final_value, rule_chain (ordered list of rule identifiers), confidence_score (float), timestamp, actor="heuristic-cascade-v0"
- Store a short human-readable rationale for non-trivial transforms (e.g., "removed parenthetical counter, expanded 'intl' -> 'international'").

Sampling & evaluation plan:
- Build small adjudicated seed: 600 records stratified by source and field length.
- Run cascade, compute precision/recall against gold for auto-accepts. Target: precision >= 0.97 for auto-accept.
- Inspect quick-review bucket: measure human adjudication time (aim < 30s per item).

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Create canonical exception list for punctuation-sensitive tokens (C++ etc.).
- [ ] Formalize mapping table storage (YAML vs DB) and propagation to downstream pipelines.
- [ ] Add rule to detect and preserve diacritics vs ASCII-fallback — when to prefer each?
- [ ] Wire small fallback ML model training pipeline and a lightweight explainability log per decision.

Notes to self (sleepy-hour ideas):
- Could use a small deterministic "policy tree" language (YAML) so non-dev reviewers can tweak priorities without PRs.
- Consider marking high-volume customers' records as "no-auto" by default to avoid upstream surprise.
- Keep auditing retention separate from transformed dataset (store deltas).

Short sample adjudication checks (to add to onboarding checklist):
- Check 50 auto-accepted entries: any suspicious normalizations?
- Verify that exception list prevented C++ -> C conversion.
- Verify that expansion mappings aren't introducing brand changes (e.g., "Intl" -> "International, Inc" should not happen).

References / links: see linked_artifacts for current tickets; add sample adjudication sheet after first run.

End of scratchpad.
